name: C++
summary: Learn modern C++ values, containers, algorithms, references, and resource ownership.

lessons.title: Program entry, values, and streams
lessons.explanation: A C++ program begins at main. Standard library names are in the std namespace. Use auto when the initializer makes its type clear and const when a variable should remain fixed.

api.name: std::cout << value
api.description: Send a formatted value to standard output.

api.name: std::string
api.description: Own an adjustable sequence of characters.

api.name: auto
api.description: Deduce the declared type from an initializer.

lessons.practice: Print a title, unit price, and quantity using explicitly typed values and an inferred total.
lessons.pitfall: Use the matching header for each standard facility you use. Transitive includes are not guaranteed.

exercise.expected: Print a label, unit price, quantity, and derived total.
exercise.completion: A new quantity changes the total while the label remains the same.

lessons.title: Conditions, loops, and functions
lessons.explanation: Use if and else for decisions. A range-for visits values in a range. A function names a reusable operation and specifies a return type.

api.name: std::array<T, N>
api.description: Store a fixed number of elements with value semantics.

api.name: for (auto value : range)
api.description: Visit each element by copying its value.

api.name: break / continue
api.description: Exit the loop or skip the rest of the current iteration.

lessons.practice: Write a function that totals values above a threshold. Use C++17 or newer for std::array deduction in this example.
lessons.pitfall: Integer division discards the fractional part. Convert an operand when you need a fractional result.

exercise.expected: Sum the values strictly above a caller-provided threshold.
exercise.completion: Values equal to the threshold are excluded, and an empty input gives zero.

lessons.title: Vectors, maps, and checked access
lessons.explanation: Use vector for contiguous resizable data and unordered_map for key-to-value lookup without sorted iteration. Use const references when reading large values without copying them.

api.name: std::vector::push_back()
api.description: Append an element to a growable array.

api.name: std::vector::at(index)
api.description: Check an index and throw std::out_of_range when it is invalid.

api.name: std::unordered_map::find(key)
api.description: Return an iterator to an entry, or end() when absent.

lessons.practice: Count characters in a short word, then print the count of a character without inserting a new key.
lessons.pitfall: Growing a vector may invalidate its iterators, pointers, and references.

exercise.expected: Count words without assuming which keys occur.
exercise.completion: Lookup of an absent word reports zero without adding it to the map.

lessons.title: References, classes, and invariants
lessons.explanation: A reference is another name for an object. Use a const reference for read-only access. A class can keep its fields private and enforce valid state through its public methods.

api.name: const T&
api.description: Pass an object by reference without permitting mutation through the reference.

api.name: method() const
api.description: Mark a method as read-only for ordinary object fields.

api.name: private
api.description: Restrict access to implementation details.

lessons.practice: Add a decrement method that rejects a negative result.
lessons.pitfall: A reference must not outlive the object it refers to.

exercise.expected: Implement a counter whose value never becomes negative.
exercise.completion: Reading uses a const reference and an attempted decrement at zero leaves it unchanged.

lessons.title: Algorithms, iterators, and lambdas
lessons.explanation: Algorithms operate over iterator ranges. The end iterator marks the position after the last element. Use a lambda to supply a short comparison or test.

api.name: std::sort(first, last)
api.description: Sort a range in place.

api.name: std::find(first, last, value)
api.description: Find the first matching value or return last.

api.name: std::count_if(first, last, predicate)
api.description: Count values that pass a test.

lessons.practice: Sort scores in descending order and count the values that fall within an inclusive range.
lessons.pitfall: A sorting comparator must report false for equal inputs. Using >= instead of > violates its ordering requirement.

exercise.expected: Count scores in an inclusive range and print them in sorted order.
exercise.completion: The first and last valid scores are included, and no score outside the range is counted.

lessons.title: RAII and ownership with unique_ptr
lessons.explanation: Tie cleanup to the lifetime of an object. Standard containers own their storage and clean it up when they go out of scope. Use unique_ptr when dynamic storage needs one explicit owner.

api.name: std::make_unique<T>(args...)
api.description: Create a dynamically allocated object with an exclusive owner.

api.name: std::unique_ptr<T>
api.description: Release the owned object automatically.

api.name: std::move(value)
api.description: Allow another operation to move from a value. The receiving operation determines what happens.

lessons.practice: Write a function returning a unique_ptr to a populated vector and print its first element.
lessons.pitfall: Prefer an ordinary value or a standard container when dynamic ownership adds no benefit.

exercise.expected: Transfer a unique pointer to a function and read it through the new owner.
exercise.completion: After transfer the original pointer is empty and the new owner reports the value.

lessons.title: Stream input, strings, and optional values
lessons.explanation: Use stream extraction to parse typed values and getline to read a whole line. Use optional when a function can meaningfully return no value.

api.name: std::getline(stream, text)
api.description: Read characters through the next newline or end of stream.

api.name: std::ifstream
api.description: Open a file stream for input and close it automatically.

api.name: std::optional<T>::value_or(fallback)
api.description: Read a value if present or return a fallback.

lessons.practice: Read one line from stdin. Parse a nonnegative int with optional surrounding whitespace.
lessons.pitfall: Check a stream operation before using an output variable. Extraction can fail.

exercise.expected: Print the parsed integer or the word invalid when the whole line is not a valid count.
exercise.completion: Check whitespace, zero, a negative number, trailing text, and a value beyond the int range.

lessons.title: Constructors, copy, and value semantics
lessons.explanation: A constructor initializes members before its body executes. When members are regular values, a default copy copies each member. A copied string or vector owns independent storage, so copying this class produces a separate value.

api.name: explicit
api.description: Prevent implicit conversion through this constructor.

api.name: member initializer list
api.description: Initialize members before executing the constructor body.

lessons.practice: Add a vector of tags and copy a book after adding two tags.
lessons.pitfall: A copied raw pointer still points to the same object. Prefer owned values when copies should be independent.

exercise.expected: Adding a new tag to the copy leaves the original tags unchanged.
exercise.completion: Print or assert each tag count before and after editing the copy.

lessons.title: Borrow strings with string_view
lessons.explanation: A string_view refers to an existing character range without copying it. A substring of the view still borrows from the original storage. Use a view when the caller keeps that storage valid for the entire use, and return an owning string when the data needs to outlive its source.

api.name: std::string_view
api.description: A non-owning view over a character range.

api.name: std::string_view::substr()
api.description: Return a subview referring to the same storage.

lessons.practice: Split two records on the first colon and copy their category labels into an owning vector.
lessons.pitfall: Do not keep a view into a temporary string or storage that can be reallocated.

exercise.expected: The stored category labels still work after the source strings go out of scope.
exercise.completion: Try a record with a colon and one without a colon.

lessons.title: Erase vector elements without invalidating iteration
lessons.explanation: remove_if moves the retained values toward the front and returns the new logical end. It does not resize the vector. Erase the trailing range to remove the elements physically. A vector modification can invalidate positions, so do not keep an iterator or reference across this operation unless you know it remains valid.

api.name: std::remove_if()
api.description: Partition retained values into the front of the range and return the retained end.

api.name: std::vector::erase()
api.description: Remove the range and reduce the vector size.

lessons.practice: Remove readings above a caller-supplied limit without reordering the remaining readings.
lessons.pitfall: Incrementing an iterator that erase invalidated is undefined behavior. Recompute it or use the iterator returned by erase.

exercise.expected: The resulting vector contains the allowed values in their original order.
exercise.completion: Test consecutive removed values, all removed, and no removals.

lessons.title: Reuse algorithms with function templates
lessons.explanation: A function template describes code parameterized by a type. Calls often deduce that type from arguments. Every operation used by the function still has to work for the deduced type. This comparison template intentionally requires both operands to have the same deduced type.

api.name: template <typename T>
api.description: Declare a template with a type parameter.

api.name: const T&
api.description: Borrow each operand for comparison without copying it just to read it.

lessons.practice: Write a template that tests whether a value lies in an inclusive range using only operator<.
lessons.pitfall: Passing an int and a double gives conflicting deductions for T. Choose a common type deliberately before calling the template.

exercise.expected: The same source handles integers and strings of the same type.
exercise.completion: Include endpoints, an out-of-range value, and a mixed-type call that should fail to compile.

lessons.title: Decompose map entries with structured bindings
lessons.explanation: A structured binding gives names to the elements of a tuple-like object or to compatible data members. Each ordered map entry is a key-value pair. Binding by reference avoids an extra copy and using const documents that the loop only reads the entries.

api.name: const auto& [key, value]
api.description: Decompose the entry through a const reference.

api.name: std::map
api.description: Store entries ordered by key using the map comparator.

lessons.practice: Summarize a small inventory in sorted key order and compute the total count.
lessons.pitfall: For an unordered_map, iteration order is unspecified. Do not base expected output on that order.

exercise.expected: Each key appears once and the final line is the sum of all values.
exercise.completion: Insert keys in reverse order and verify the output ordering stays the same.

lessons.title: Sort records with a consistent comparison
lessons.explanation: A sort comparison answers whether its left argument belongs strictly before its right. Compare primary keys first and use a secondary key for ties. std::tie makes tuples of references so their lexicographic comparison can express a two-key order.

api.name: std::tie()
api.description: Build a tuple of lvalue references for lexicographic comparison.

api.name: std::stable_sort()
api.description: Keep the relative order of elements that compare equivalent.

lessons.practice: Sort a list of assignments by due day and then by title.
lessons.pitfall: A comparison using <= incorrectly says that equivalent values precede each other.

exercise.expected: Assignments on the same day are ordered by title.
exercise.completion: Include two assignments with the same day and check that comparing a record with itself returns false.

lessons.title: Represent a value or error with variant
lessons.explanation: A variant stores exactly one of a fixed set of alternatives when constructed normally, and a failed type-changing operation can leave it valueless. A parser can return a result or an error description without using a sentinel number that could be mistaken for data. Inspect the active alternative before reading its value.

api.name: std::variant<T, U>
api.description: Store a value tagged with its active alternative.

api.name: std::get_if<T>()
api.description: Return a pointer to the requested alternative, or a null pointer when it is absent.

lessons.practice: Return a score or an explanatory error when parsing text with a bounded acceptable range.
lessons.pitfall: std::get throws std::bad_variant_access when the requested alternative is not active.

exercise.expected: Distinguish malformed text from a valid integer that is out of bounds.
exercise.completion: Try 0, 100, 101, and a token with trailing letters.

lessons.title: Build a sorted index and find an insertion point
lessons.explanation: lower_bound finds the first position whose element is not less than a key. This can be an exact match, the next greater element, or the end. Reusing the order from sorting is necessary for correct binary search.

api.name: std::lower_bound()
api.description: Find the start of the portion that does not compare less than the search key.

api.name: range.end()
api.description: Represent the position just past the last valid element.

lessons.practice: Extend the search to insert missing titles at the returned position.
lessons.pitfall: A returned position inside the range does not imply a match. Compare the key before reporting a result.

exercise.expected: A missing title is inserted while an existing title does not create a duplicate.
exercise.completion: Insert a title at the start and at the end, then repeat a known title and verify the size is unchanged.

prerequisites: Know how to save a plain text file.
To run the examples, install a C++17 compiler and standard library such as Clang with libc++ or GCC with libstdc++.
metadata.miniProject: Build a local book index. Store title and author values, provide a case-sensitive title search, and sort results deterministically by title and author. Exercise an empty catalog and equal titles.
